question: I have an Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan card and am visiting another Canadian province. What must you confirm before assuring me that a particular medical service will be paid?
generated_answer:
You must verify that I have not been outside of Alberta for more than 182 days in a 12 month period immediately preceding the first day of the hospitalization. If you find that I have been outside Alberta for longer than this timeframe, you must first contact the Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan at (403) 297-7301, or 1-800-427-3668. Alberta Health and Wellness will then contact me to determine my residency and confirm my eligibility. 5.4 Prior Approval Requirement

Are there any prior approval requirements for insured hospital services? No. 5.5 Accessibility

The Alberta Health Care Insurance Act, section 9, prohibits extra-billing by facilities providing insured services. Section 11 of the Act prohibits any person from paying to obtain an insured service. Accessibility Standards

Are there written client accessibility standards that you apply? Yes. The Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan meets all Accessibility Standards. Exclusion criteria are clearly outlined in the program's policies. 6.0 Uninsured Hospital, Physician and Surgical-Dental Services

6.1 Uninsured Hospital Services

Dental services; (however, if a patient is hospitalized for a dental condition or dental service is required in conjunction with other insured hospital procedures, it is insured); and

Physiotherapy, psychology and other diagnostic and treatment services provided by other than a physician or as part of an insured service; (however, these services may be reimbursed when provided in conjunction with an insured in-patient or out-patient hospital service). A detailed listing of uninsured services is contained in the Schedule of Medical Benefits. The Schedule is approved by the Minister of Health and Wellness and is amended from time-to-time. The Schedule is available on the Alberta Health website at: http://www.health.alberta.ca/services.html. 6.2 Uninsured Physician Services

Physician services not covered by the Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan are listed in the Schedule of Medical Benefits. The Schedule is approved by the Minister of Health and Wellness and is amended from time-to-time. The Schedule is available on the Alberta Health website at: http://www.health.alberta.ca/services.html. The Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan funds a number of services that would otherwise be uninsured. Funding is provided for the following services:

Services provided by a physician in conjunction with an insured service; and

Services provided by a physician in order to treat an insured condition. 6.3 Uninsured Surgical-Dental Services

Dental services when the condition is not related to an oral and maxillofacial abnormality or disease;

Services related to the extraction of third molars where the service does not require the use of an operating theatre or the patient is not hospitalized; and

Oral surgery services not covered by the Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan are listed in the Schedule of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery Benefits. The Schedule is approved by the Minister of Health and Wellness and is amended from time-to-time. The Schedule is available on the Alberta Health website at: http://www.health.alberta.ca/services.html. The Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan funds a number of services that would otherwise be uninsured. Funding is provided for the following services:

Services provided by a dentist in conjunction with an insured service; and

Services provided by a dentist in order to treat an insured condition. 7.0 Uninsured Hospital, Physician and Surgical-Dental Services Under the Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan - Private Facilities

There are no charges allowed in Alberta for medically necessary hospital, physician or surgical-dental services. Medically necessary hospital, physician and surgical-dental services are provided through the Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan. 7.1 Uninsured Hospital Services

Dental services; (however, if a patient is hospitalized for a dental condition or dental service is required in conjunction with other insured hospital procedures, it is insured); and

Dental services when the condition is not related to an oral and maxillofacial abnormality or disease;

Services related to the extraction of third molars where the service does not require the use of an operating theatre or the patient is not hospitalized; and

Oral surgery services not covered by the Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan are listed in the Schedule of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery Benefits. 8.0 Accessibility
